html:
The Chahamanas of Shakambhari, better known as the Chauhans, were a Rajput dynasty that ruled part of what is now Rajasthan, in north-western India, from about the 600s to 1194. The map shows them from 600 to 1100.

Their early seat was Shakambhari, the town of Sambhar by a large salt lake. For a long time they served as vassals of the Gurjara-Pratiharas. As the Pratiharas weakened in the 900s, the Chauhans became independent and expanded. In the early 1100s Ajayaraja II founded Ajmer and made it the capital. In the 1100s Vigraharaja IV took Delhi.

Their most famous king was Prithviraj Chauhan. He beat Muhammad of Ghor at the first battle of Tarain in 1191, but lost to him at the second battle in 1192 and was killed. The defeat opened north India to the Ghurids and led to the Delhi Sultanate. Prithviraj became a hero of later Rajput ballads. Branches of the family went on ruling smaller states such as Ranthambore.
